questions.stem: Listen to the station announcement. What is happening?
options: A train to Osaka is arriving at platform 3
A train from Osaka is arriving at platform 3
A train to Osaka is leaving from platform 2
The train to Osaka at platform 3 is running late
questions.explanation: You heard 「まもなく、三ばんせんに、おおさか行きの電車がまいります。」 「おおさか行き」 means bound for Osaka, not coming from it, and 「まいります」 is the humble form of 「来ます」 that announcements use for a train arriving.

audio.text: まもなく、三ばんせんに、おおさか行きの電車がまいります。

questions.stem: Listen to the announcement in a shop. When does the shop close today?
questions.explanation: You heard 「この店は、本日、午後八時にしまります。」 「午後」 is the afternoon and evening, so this is 8 pm; 「午前」 would have made it the morning. 「本日」 is the formal word for today.

audio.text: ご来店ありがとうございます。この店は、本日、午後八時にしまります。

questions.stem: Listen to the school announcement. What will happen tomorrow?
options: The sports carnival will be held indoors in the rain
The sports carnival will start once the rain stops
The sports carnival will go ahead even if it rains
The sports carnival is off because rain is forecast
questions.explanation: You heard that rain is forecast (「雨のよほう」), so 「スポーツ大会はありません」 - there will be no sports carnival. Nothing was said about moving it indoors or starting late.

audio.text: みなさん、あしたは雨のよほうなので、スポーツ大会はありません。

questions.stem: Listen to the weather forecast. What will tomorrow be like?
options: Fine all day, with rain at night
Rain in the morning, fine in the afternoon
Fine in the morning, rain in the afternoon
Rain all day, clearing in the evening
questions.explanation: You heard 「朝は雨ですが、午後ははれるでしょう。」 「朝」 is the morning and 「はれる」 means to clear up and be fine. The order of 朝 and 午後 is what separates the answer from its mirror image.

audio.text: あしたの天気です。朝は雨ですが、午後ははれるでしょう。

questions.stem: Listen to the platform announcement. What is the problem?
questions.explanation: You heard 「電車がおくれています」 - the train is running late - followed by the standard formal apology 「もうしわけありません」.

audio.text: 電車がおくれています。ごめいわくをおかけして、もうしわけありません。

questions.stem: Listen to the library rule. What is not allowed?
questions.explanation: You heard 「食べたり飲んだりしてはいけません」. 「〜たり〜たり」 lists actions as examples, and 「〜てはいけません」 says they are not allowed.

audio.text: としょかんの中で、食べたり飲んだりしてはいけません。

questions.stem: Listen to the museum guide. What is the rule about photos?
options: Photos are allowed only with a flash
Photos are fine, but not with a flash
No photos are allowed anywhere here
questions.explanation: You heard 「しゃしんをとってもいいですが、フラッシュはだめです」. 「〜てもいいです」 gives permission, and the 「が」 ('but') introduces the exception: 「だめ」 means not allowed.

audio.text: ここでしゃしんをとってもいいですが、フラッシュはだめです。

questions.stem: Listen to the phone message. Why is Tanaka calling?
options: To ask you what time tomorrow's party starts
To say they will be late to tomorrow's party
To say they can't come to the party tomorrow
To invite you to a party at their place tomorrow
questions.explanation: You heard 「あしたのパーティーですが、行けなくなりました」. 「行けなくなりました」 means 'it has turned out I can't go', and the 「すみません」 that follows is the apology.

audio.text: もしもし、田中です。あしたのパーティーですが、行けなくなりました。すみません。

questions.stem: Listen to the phone call. Where is the caller now?
questions.explanation: You heard 「今、駅にいるから」 - 'I'm at the station now, so'. The caller then says they will get home around seven, in the casual speech used with family.

audio.text: もしもし、お母さん？今、駅にいるから、七時ごろ家に帰るね。

questions.stem: Listen to the message about tennis practice. What has changed?
options: It has moved from tomorrow to today
It now starts at ten, not nine
It now starts at nine, not ten
It now finishes at ten, not nine
questions.explanation: You heard 「九時からじゃなくて、十時からになりました」. 「AじゃなくてB」 means 'not A but B', and 「〜になりました」 marks the change, so the new time is ten.

audio.text: もしもし、すずきです。あしたのテニスのれんしゅうは、九時からじゃなくて、十時からになりました。

questions.stem: Listen to the reply to an invitation. What does the speaker mean?
options: They will be a little late on Saturday
They will give you an answer on Saturday
Saturday doesn't suit them: a polite no
They can come on Saturday for a short while
questions.explanation: You heard 「土曜日はちょっと…」. Leaving the sentence unfinished after 「ちょっと」 is the usual polite way to say no; the listener understands the refusal without it being spoken. It does not mean 'a little while'.

audio.text: あ、土曜日はちょっと…。

questions.stem: Listen to how the speaker answers an invitation. How do they respond?
questions.explanation: You heard 「いいですね。ぜひ行きたいです。」 「ぜひ」 means 'by all means', so this is a keen yes.

audio.text: いいですね。ぜひ行きたいです。

questions.stem: Listen. Why can't the speaker accept the invitation?
options: They are visiting family that day
They are not well that day
They have a part-time job that day
They have a test that day
questions.explanation: You heard 「その日はアルバイトがあるんです」. 「アルバイト」 is a part-time job, and the 「んです」 ending gives it as the explanation for saying no.

audio.text: ざんねんですが、その日はアルバイトがあるんです。

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker suggest?
questions.explanation: You heard 「日曜日はだめですが、土曜日はどうですか。」 Sunday is no good, and 「〜はどうですか」 offers Saturday instead.

audio.text: 日曜日はだめですが、土曜日はどうですか。

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker doing?
options: Saying they saw a film at the weekend
Inviting someone to a film this weekend
Asking if someone saw a film last weekend
Saying they don't want to see a film
questions.explanation: You heard 「いっしょにえいがを見に行きませんか」. A negative question with 「〜ませんか」 is an invitation, not a question about the past, and 「こんどのしゅうまつ」 is the coming weekend.

audio.text: こんどのしゅうまつ、いっしょにえいがを見に行きませんか。

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker do every morning?
options: Walks the dog at six in the evening
Gets up at six and walks the dog
Gets up at seven and walks the dog
Gets up at six and feeds the cat
questions.explanation: You heard 「毎朝六時に起きて、犬とさんぽします」. 「毎朝」 is every morning, and the て-form joins the two actions in order.

audio.text: 私は毎朝六時に起きて、犬とさんぽします。

questions.stem: Listen. Why did the speaker miss school yesterday?
questions.explanation: You heard 「あたまがいたかったので」 - 'because my head hurt'. 「ので」 gives the reason, and 「学校を休みました」 means they stayed away from school.

audio.text: きのうはあたまがいたかったので、学校を休みました。

questions.stem: Listen. Who lives in Sapporo?
questions.explanation: You heard 「兄は大学生で、今、さっぽろにすんでいます」. 「兄」 is the speaker's own older brother; an older sister would be 「姉」 and a younger brother 「弟」.

audio.text: 兄は大学生で、今、さっぽろにすんでいます。

questions.stem: Listen to the shop assistant. How much is the T-shirt?
questions.explanation: You heard 「二千五百円」 - two thousand five hundred yen. Japanese counts thousands with 「千」 and hundreds with 「百」, just as the kanji are written.

audio.text: このTシャツは二千五百円です。

questions.stem: Listen. What is the price of the bag?
questions.explanation: You heard 「一万八千円」. Japanese groups large numbers in ten-thousands, so 「一万」 is 10,000 and 「八千」 adds 8,000. This is why big numbers need listening practice: English groups in thousands.

audio.text: このかばんは一万八千円です。

questions.stem: Listen to the directions. What should you do?
options: Leave the station and turn left
Leave the station and go straight on
Leave the station and turn right
questions.explanation: You heard 「駅を出て、右にまがってください」. 「右」 is right and 「左」 would be left; 「まっすぐ」 would mean straight ahead.

audio.text: 駅を出て、右にまがってください。

questions.stem: Listen. Where is the bookshop?
questions.explanation: You heard 「本やは駅の前にあります」. 「前」 is in front; behind would be 「うしろ」 and next to 「となり」.

audio.text: 本やは駅の前にあります。

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say about Japan?
options: They went there three years ago
They will go there in three months
They want to go there three times
They have been there three times
questions.explanation: You heard 「三かい行ったことがあります」. 「〜たことがあります」 talks about experience, and 「かい」 counts times, not years.

audio.text: 私は日本に三かい行ったことがあります。

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say about the train?
options: Faster than the bus, and cheaper
Slower than the bus, and dearer
Faster than the bus, but dearer
Slower than the bus, but cheaper
questions.explanation: You heard 「電車はバスよりはやいですが、高いです」. 「AはBより〜」 says A is more so than B, and the 「が」 sets up the drawback: it costs more.

audio.text: 電車はバスよりはやいですが、高いです。

questions.stem: Listen. Which season does the speaker like better?
questions.explanation: You heard 「春も好きですが、秋のほうが好きです」. 「〜のほうが好き」 marks the preferred one, so autumn wins even though spring is mentioned first.

audio.text: 春も好きですが、秋のほうが好きです。

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker's favourite subject?
questions.explanation: You heard 「いちばん好きなかもくは英語です」. 「いちばん」 makes it the favourite, and 「英語」 is English; Japanese would be 「日本語」.

audio.text: いちばん好きなかもくは英語です。

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker want to do in the future?
questions.explanation: You heard 「しょうらい、日本で英語をおしえたいです」. 「おしえる」 is to teach (to study would be 「べんきょうする」), and 「日本で」 sets it in Japan.

audio.text: しょうらい、日本で英語をおしえたいです。

questions.stem: Listen. Why does the speaker like the town?
questions.explanation: You heard 「この町はしずかできれいだから、好きです」. 「しずか」 is quiet, 「きれい」 clean or pretty, and 「から」 marks them as the reason.

audio.text: この町はしずかできれいだから、好きです。

questions.stem: Listen. What is Yumi doing now?
options: Waiting for a friend at the station
Meeting a friend at a shop
Walking to the station with a friend
Waiting for a train at the station
questions.explanation: You heard 「駅で友だちをまっています」. 「〜ています」 is happening now, and 「友だちをまつ」 is to wait for a friend, not for a train.

audio.text: ゆみさんは今、駅で友だちをまっています。

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker asking?
options: For someone to close the window
Whether they may open the window
For someone to open the window
Whether the window is already open
questions.explanation: You heard 「まどをあけてもいいですか」. 「〜てもいいですか」 asks permission for yourself; asking someone else to do it would be 「あけてください」.

audio.text: すみません、まどをあけてもいいですか。

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker tell the driver?
options: Driving fast here is not allowed
questions.explanation: You heard 「ここに車をとめてはいけません」. 「とめる」 is to stop or park, and 「〜てはいけません」 forbids it.

audio.text: ここに車をとめてはいけません。

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker say about the homework?
options: It must be handed in by tomorrow
It needn't be done by tomorrow
It will be handed out tomorrow
It must be finished by today
questions.explanation: You heard 「あしたまでに、しゅくだいを出さなければなりません」. 「〜までに」 is 'by', and 「〜なければなりません」 means must. The double negative is easy to mishear as 'doesn't have to'.

audio.text: あしたまでに、しゅくだいを出さなければなりません。

questions.stem: Listen. What does the speaker do at weekends?
options: Watches films and goes out with friends
Reads books and stays home with family
Reads books and goes out with friends
Reads books and plays sport with friends
questions.explanation: You heard 「本を読んだり、友だちと出かけたりします」. 「〜たり〜たり」 gives examples of what they do, here reading and going out with friends.

audio.text: しゅうまつは、本を読んだり、友だちと出かけたりします。

questions.stem: Listen. When does the film start?
questions.explanation: You heard 「午後三時半」. 「半」 adds the half hour, and 「三時」 is three; four would be 「四時」 (よじ).

audio.text: えいがは午後三時半にはじまります。

questions.stem: Listen. When is the test?
questions.explanation: You heard 「来週の水曜日」. 「来週」 is next week (this week is 「今週」, last week 「先週」), and 「水曜日」 is Wednesday; Thursday is 「木曜日」.

audio.text: テストは来週の水曜日です。

questions.stem: Listen to the restaurant worker. What are they asking?
options: How many people are in your group
What you would like to order
questions.explanation: You heard 「何名さまですか」. 「名」 counts people politely, so this asks how many are in your party - the first question in most restaurants.

audio.text: いらっしゃいませ。何名さまですか。

questions.stem: Listen. What is the customer asking for?
questions.explanation: You heard 「もう少し安いのはありますか」. 「安い」 is cheap, and 「もう少し」 means 'a little more', so they want something cheaper.

audio.text: すみません、もう少し安いのはありますか。

questions.stem: Listen to the doctor. What advice is given?
options: Rest, but don't take any medicine
Drink water and get some exercise
Take medicine and get plenty of rest
Take medicine and go back to school
questions.explanation: You heard 「くすりを飲んで、ゆっくり休んでください」. Medicine is 'drunk' in Japanese (「くすりを飲む」), and 「ゆっくり休む」 is to rest properly.

audio.text: かぜですね。くすりを飲んで、ゆっくり休んでください。

questions.stem: Listen. What is the speaker's opinion of the book?
questions.explanation: You heard 「おもしろいと思いますが、ちょっと長いです」. 「〜と思います」 gives the opinion and 「が」 adds the reservation: a little long.

audio.text: この本はおもしろいと思いますが、ちょっと長いです。

questions.stem: Listen. What did the speaker do in the summer holidays?
options: Had their grandmother come to stay
questions.explanation: You heard 「家族とメルボルンへ行って、おばあさんに会いました」. 「おばあさん」 is grandmother (an aunt is 「おばさん」, one long vowel shorter), and the family went to Melbourne.

audio.text: 夏休みに家族とメルボルンへ行って、おばあさんに会いました。

questions.stem: Listen to the listener's response. What does it show?
questions.explanation: You heard 「へえ、そうなんですか。」 This is あいづち: a short response that shows you are following and interested. 「へえ」 adds a note of surprise.

audio.text: へえ、そうなんですか。

questions.stem: Someone has just praised the speaker's Japanese. Listen to the reply. What does it mean?
options: No, I still have a long way to go
Yes, I have studied it for years
No, I don't speak Japanese at all
Thank you, I am very good at it
questions.explanation: You heard 「いいえ、まだまだです。」 Deflecting praise like this is the usual modest reply; 「まだまだ」 means 'not yet, still far from it'.

audio.text: いいえ、まだまだです。

questions.stem: Listen. Why was the speaker late?
questions.explanation: You heard 「おそくなってすみません。電車がおくれたんです。」 「おくれる」 is to be late or delayed, and the subject is the train.

audio.text: おそくなってすみません。電車がおくれたんです。

questions.stem: Listen. How does the speaker get to school, and how long does it take?
questions.explanation: You heard 「バスで二十分ぐらいかかります」. 「で」 marks the means of transport, 「二十分」 is twenty minutes, and 「ぐらい」 means about.

audio.text: 家から学校まで、バスで二十分ぐらいかかります。

questions.stem: Listen to the English, then choose the Japanese.
options: 日本に行くことがあります。
日本に行ったことがありません。
日本に行ってみたいです。
日本に行ったことがあります。
questions.explanation: 'I have been to Japan' is an experience, so it takes the past plain form plus 「ことがあります」. With the dictionary form, 「行くことがあります」 means 'I sometimes go'.

audio.text: I have been to Japan.

questions.stem: Listen to the English and choose the Japanese for it.
options: ここにすわってください。
ここにすわりましたか。
ここにすわってもいいですか。
ここにすわってはいけません。
questions.explanation: 'May I sit here?' asks permission: て-form plus 「もいいですか」. 「すわってください」 would tell someone else to sit.

audio.text: May I sit here?

questions.stem: Listen to the English sentence, then choose the Japanese.
options: ろうかをはしりませんでした。
ろうかをはしってはいけません。
ろうかをはしってもいいです。
ろうかをはしってください。
questions.explanation: 'You must not run in the corridor' is a prohibition: て-form plus 「はいけません」. 「〜てもいいです」 is the opposite, giving permission.

audio.text: You must not run in the corridor.

questions.stem: Listen to the English, then pick the matching Japanese.
options: あしたは雨がふったと思います。
あしたは雨がふりたいです。
あしたは雨がふりませんでした。
あしたは雨がふると思います。
questions.explanation: 'I think it will rain tomorrow' needs the plain non-past 「ふる」 before 「と思います」. The past 「ふった」 cannot go with 「あした」, and 「〜たい」 is for wanting, which rain cannot do.

audio.text: I think it will rain tomorrow.

questions.stem: Listen to the English, then choose the right Japanese.
options: 駅で会いませんでした。
questions.explanation: 'Shall we meet at the station?' is 「〜ましょうか」, and the place where meeting happens takes 「で」. 「駅に会う」 uses the particle for a destination.

audio.text: Shall we meet at the station?

questions.stem: Listen, then choose what it means.
questions.explanation: You heard 「先週」, which means 'last week'. The other options are also time expressions, so the choice turns on hearing this one rather than on ruling the others out.

audio.text: 先週

questions.stem: Listen. Which of these did you hear?
questions.explanation: 「来週」 is what was said, and it means 'next week'. Matching a sound to its written form is harder than choosing a meaning, because all four options belong to the same group and several of them sound alike.

audio.text: 来週

questions.stem: Listen, then choose what it means.
questions.explanation: You heard 「今週」, which means 'this week'. The other options are also time expressions, so the choice turns on hearing this one rather than on ruling the others out.

audio.text: 今週

questions.stem: Listen. Which of these did you hear?
questions.explanation: 「毎週」 is what was said, and it means 'every week'. Matching a sound to its written form is harder than choosing a meaning, because all four options belong to the same group and several of them sound alike.

audio.text: 毎週

questions.stem: Listen, then choose what it means.
questions.explanation: You heard 「先月」, which means 'last month'. The other options are also time expressions, so the choice turns on hearing this one rather than on ruling the others out.

audio.text: 先月

questions.stem: Listen. Which of these did you hear?
questions.explanation: 「来月」 is what was said, and it means 'next month'. Matching a sound to its written form is harder than choosing a meaning, because all four options belong to the same group and several of them sound alike.

audio.text: 来月

questions.stem: Listen, then choose what it means.
questions.explanation: You heard 「来年」, which means 'next year'. The other options are also time expressions, so the choice turns on hearing this one rather than on ruling the others out.

audio.text: 来年

questions.stem: Listen. Which of these did you hear?
questions.explanation: 「毎晩」 is what was said, and it means 'every night'. Matching a sound to its written form is harder than choosing a meaning, because all four options belong to the same group and several of them sound alike.

audio.text: 毎晩

questions.stem: Listen, then choose what it means.
questions.explanation: You heard 「少しまってください。」, which means 'please wait a moment'. The other options are also requests with 〜てください, so the choice turns on hearing this one rather than on ruling the others out.

audio.text: 少しまってください。

questions.stem: Listen. Which of these did you hear?
options: こちらを見てください。
ここに名前を書いてください。
この文を読んでください。
questions.explanation: 「ここに名前を書いてください。」 is what was said, and it means 'please write your name here'. Matching a sound to its written form is harder than choosing a meaning, because all four options belong to the same group and several of them sound alike.

audio.text: ここに名前を書いてください。

questions.stem: Listen, then choose what it means.
questions.explanation: You heard 「この文を読んでください。」, which means 'please read this sentence'. The other options are also requests with 〜てください, so the choice turns on hearing this one rather than on ruling the others out.

audio.text: この文を読んでください。

questions.stem: Listen. Which of these did you hear?
options: こちらを見てください。
もういちど言ってください。
ゆっくり話してください。
questions.explanation: 「よく聞いてください。」 is what was said, and it means 'please listen carefully'. Matching a sound to its written form is harder than choosing a meaning, because all four options belong to the same group and several of them sound alike.

audio.text: よく聞いてください。

questions.stem: Listen, then choose what it means.
questions.explanation: You heard 「こちらを見てください。」, which means 'please look this way'. The other options are also requests with 〜てください, so the choice turns on hearing this one rather than on ruling the others out.

audio.text: こちらを見てください。

questions.stem: Listen. Which of these did you hear?
options: もういちど言ってください。
ゆっくり話してください。
questions.explanation: 「もういちど言ってください。」 is what was said, and it means 'please say it again'. Matching a sound to its written form is harder than choosing a meaning, because all four options belong to the same group and several of them sound alike.

audio.text: もういちど言ってください。

questions.stem: Listen, then choose what it means.
questions.explanation: You heard 「ゆっくり話してください。」, which means 'please speak slowly'. The other options are also requests with 〜てください, so the choice turns on hearing this one rather than on ruling the others out.

audio.text: ゆっくり話してください。

questions.stem: Listen. Which of these did you hear?
options: ここに名前を書いてください。
この文を読んでください。
questions.explanation: 「早く来てください。」 is what was said, and it means 'please come quickly'. Matching a sound to its written form is harder than choosing a meaning, because all four options belong to the same group and several of them sound alike.

audio.text: 早く来てください。

questions.stem: Listen, then choose what it means.
questions.explanation: You heard 「しゃしんをとってもいいですか。」, which means 'may I take a photo?'. The other options are also permission and prohibition phrases, so the choice turns on hearing this one rather than on ruling the others out.

audio.text: しゃしんをとってもいいですか。

questions.stem: Listen. Which of these did you hear?
options: 早く帰ってもいいですか。
ここで食べてはいけません。
はいってもいいですよ。
ここでおよいではいけません。
questions.explanation: 「ここで食べてはいけません。」 is what was said, and it means 'you must not eat here'. Matching a sound to its written form is harder than choosing a meaning, because all four options belong to the same group and several of them sound alike.

audio.text: ここで食べてはいけません。

questions.stem: Listen, then choose what it means.
questions.explanation: You heard 「はいってもいいですよ。」, which means 'you may come in'. The other options are also permission and prohibition phrases, so the choice turns on hearing this one rather than on ruling the others out.

audio.text: はいってもいいですよ。

questions.stem: Listen. Which of these did you hear?
options: 早く帰ってもいいですか。
大きいこえで話してはいけません。
しゃしんをとってもいいですか。
ここでおよいではいけません。
questions.explanation: 「ここでおよいではいけません。」 is what was said, and it means 'you must not swim here'. Matching a sound to its written form is harder than choosing a meaning, because all four options belong to the same group and several of them sound alike.
